lostIntro: Act quickly, but stay calm. These are the first steps; the links go to the official registers (Snuffel doesn't pass anything on).
lostStep1: Don't chase your dog or call loudly: a frightened dog runs further, and may even avoid you. Have someone wait where it went missing, and leave something there that smells of home (a blanket, worn clothes, water).
lostStep2: Report it missing straight away in the national register and with the chip registry: mark your dog as missing and check that your phone number is right.
lostStep3: Tell the animal ambulance, nearby shelters and vets, and the municipality or police. Found dogs often end up there.
lostStep4: Share a recent photo on local social media and on posters. Search calmly at dawn and dusk, when frightened dogs move about. Keep checking the found reports.
lostStep5: Watch out for scams: never pay anyone up front to “find” your dog, and don't post the chip number publicly.
foundStep1: Keep your distance if the dog is scared and don't chase it. Is it injured, or was it hit by a car? Find an open vet now.
foundStep2: Have the chip read by a vet or a shelter; that is usually free. That is how the owner is found.
foundStep3: Report the found dog in the national register or to the municipality.
foundStep4: Keep the dog safe until the owner is found, and only hand it over with proof: the chip registration, vaccination booklet or photos.
lostOtherNote: In other countries: report it to the national pet register or the municipality. Europetnet looks up chip numbers in registers across Europe.
